question.knowledge_point: Expressing a Complex Number in Polar Form
question.problem: Express $z=5+12\text{i}$ in the form $r(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).$ Give $\theta $ in radians to three decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=5+12\text{i},$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169} \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=5$ is positive and $y=12$ is positive, $z$ lies in the first quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{12}{5}) \\  & ≈1.176,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. 

Finally, we write the complex number $z=5+12\text{i}$ in polar form:

$$
z=13(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.176)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(1.176))
$$
